problem: ImageNav is scored by a coarse 1 m stop criterion, so existing modular (semantic-similarity-threshold) and end-to-end methods cannot recover the exact 6-DoF goal camera pose needed for manipulation. The closest prior work, GauScoreMap, needs a pre-built Gaussian Splatting scene.
motivation: A robot grasping an object from a reference photo must reach the exact position and heading where the photo was taken. Semantic matching cannot give a precise pose, while 3D multi-view foundation models give dense correspondences and relative poses in one forward pass without scene reconstruction or scene-specific training.
key_idea: Treat the goal image as a geometric query: a DINOv2 BEV relevance signal guides exploration and gates a 3D multi-view foundation model (VGGT/Pi3), whose internal confidence self-certifies registration and recovers the goal 6-DoF pose.
insight: The foundation model's internal cross-frame attention/feature confidence works as a training-free commitment signal. Ablations show the confidence-monitored refinement loop matters (w/o it SR drops 82.6 to 77.2 and position error rises 0.21 to 1.25 m), and DINOv2 dense features beat CLIP (SR 75.7). Over-rejecting (tau=0.15) hurts more than premature acceptance (tau=0.05). SPL is low because the agent must travel to collect enough long-memory views for a well-conditioned Sim(3) alignment.
method: BEV relevance map: per-pixel DINOv2 cosine similarity between the current frame and the goal image, compressed to a ray vector with Gaussian row weighting, cos^2 FOV mask and depth truncation, then accumulated into a global BEV map (VLFM-style)
Gated frontier scoring: score = w_s*S + (1-S_norm)*(w_d*D + w_h*H) + w_e*E, with tanh normalization, so strong semantic evidence suppresses efficiency terms (w_s=0.60, w_d=0.55, w_h=0.35, w_e=0.10)
Local policy: FMM with a hard EDT exclusion zone and a graded obstacle-clearance bonus to avoid narrow-passage entrapment

Proximity gate + geometric verification: when max relevance s_rel > theta (0.0014), a short-memory window plus the goal image go to VGGT; confidence s_conf = 0.5*normalized attention + 0.5*normalized feature similarity (following RobustVGGT), accept if s_conf > tau

Last-meter localization: the long-memory cache (K frames spanning at least 3 positions) plus the goal image go to Pi3 in one pass; Umeyama Sim(3) alignment, orientation correction around the centroid, then the transform is applied to the goal pose
Confidence-monitored refinement: s_conf is re-evaluated each step and localization is re-run whenever s_conf exceeds its running best, updating the goal pose as the agent approaches

setting.backbone: DINOv2 (frozen) for relevance, VGGT (frozen) for verification, Pi3 (frozen) for pose estimation
setting.action_space: frontier-based exploration with FMM local planner producing low-level discrete actions
setting.privileged: none (uses simulator depth and odometry/pose as standard sensor inputs)

results: AnyImageNav reaches SR 93.1% on Gibson ImageNav (vs REGNav 92.9%) and 82.6% on HM3D instance ImageNav (vs GauScoreMap 78.4%), while cutting position/heading error to 0.27 m/3.41° and 0.21 m/1.23°, versus REGNav's 0.50 m/10.22° on Gibson and IEVE's 2.46 m/20.31° on HM3D. SPL is much lower than the best baselines (0.410 vs 0.671 on Gibson; 0.259 vs 0.605 on HM3D).
limitations: Relies on depth and odometry; streaming 3D models were tested but suffer temporal pose drift
Low SPL, since the agent must travel to gather viewpoint diversity before committing; 174 HM3D failures are dominated by wrong pose estimation (31.6%) and goal not found (26.4%)
Fixed thresholds theta and tau cause premature acceptance (15.0%) and wrong rejection (7.5%); pose metrics were computed only for open-source baselines
